basics.name: Zhimu Zhou
basics.label: Ph.D. Student
basics.summary: Ph.D. student at Shanghai Jiao Tong University. Researching VLA, embodied AI, HRI, and multimodal models.

education.institution: Shanghai Jiao Tong University · School of Artificial Intelligence
Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications
education.area: B.Eng. in Internet of Things Engineering

highlights: Developed VLA and World Action Model (WAM) algorithms through model adaptation, training, simulation, and real-robot evaluation.
Integrated multi-view observations, robot states, action prediction, and control for rigid parcel flipping, flexible parcel handling, and carton folding.
Compared models, analyzed failures, and iterated training based on success rate, generalization, and runtime stability.
Independently designed and implemented a machine-learning-based Post-Eval framework for multi-turn agents, automating evaluation and reducing manual work.
Deployed the framework as a core departmental tool for continuous agent evaluation in daily production.

publications.name: Duo: Dual-arm coordination for Bimanual Policies
publications.summary: Arm-wise state and action tokens with coupled generation in a shared Transformer, improving bimanual VLA and WAM policies.

publications.name: MSNav: Zero-Shot Vision-and-Language Navigation with Dynamic Memory and LLM Spatial Reasoning
publications.publisher: IEEE International Conference on Acoustics, Speech and Signal Processing (ICASSP)
publications.summary: A modular framework combining dynamic map memory, spatial reasoning, and LLM-based decision making for zero-shot vision-and-language navigation.

publications.name: Probing Visual Planning in Image Editing Models
publications.summary: EAR reframes visual planning as a single-step image transformation and introduces AMAZE, a procedurally generated benchmark of abstract planning puzzles.

publications.name: TTF-VLA: Temporal Token Fusion via Pixel-Attention Integration for Vision-Language-Action Models
publications.publisher: The Fortieth AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence (AAAI-26)
publications.summary: A training-free temporal token fusion approach that improves VLA inference by selectively integrating historical and current visual representations.

publications.name: GenPRM: Scaling Test-Time Compute of Process Reward Models via Generative Reasoning
publications.publisher: The Fortieth AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence (AAAI-26)
publications.summary: A generative process reward model that performs explicit chain-of-thought reasoning and code verification before judging each reasoning step.
